lessons.title: Orientation & exam map
lessons.objective: Understand the exam purpose, sections, question styles and a practical preparation workflow.
lessons.core_teaching_content: This lesson introduces orientation & exam map for TNPSC Group I. Start with a tutor-led explanation of the exam relevance, then model two representative examples. Learners should identify the rule or method, solve guided questions, and explain why each answer is correct. Emphasise accuracy before speed and maintain an error log for questions answered incorrectly or by guessing.
examples: Example A: Tutor demonstrates one TNPSC Group I style question and verbalises the reasoning.
Example B: Learner solves a similar question independently and compares the method with the model.
Transfer example: Change one condition and ask the learner to explain whether the same method still works.
lessons.practical_activity: Timed 8-question practice: 4 guided, 3 independent and 1 challenge question.
lessons.guided_practice: Tutor solves the first two questions with the learner, prompting the learner to state the rule before calculating or selecting an answer.
lessons.independent_practice: Complete the remaining questions without notes; mark each answer as Sure / Unsure / Guess.
questions: What is the main idea behind orientation & exam map?
Which step is easiest to get wrong, and how will you check it?
Solve one new question and explain your reasoning in complete sentences.
What mistake did you make or nearly make today?
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: 8-question checkpoint; target 75% accuracy, with every wrong answer corrected in the error log.
lessons.student_task: Create a one-page revision note containing the key rule/method, two worked examples and three self-test questions.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Model thinking rather than only answers; ask learners to justify choices; record recurring misconceptions and adjust the next practice set.
lessons.reflection_completion: Write: Today I understood ____. I need more practice on ____. My next improvement step is ____.

lessons.core_teaching_content: In School Tuition – 11th, this lesson develops review & retrieval. Teach the concept from simple to more complex examples. Use retrieval questions, worked examples and guided practice before independent work. Ask learners to explain their reasoning, not merely produce an answer.
examples: Worked example: Tutor demonstrates the process and highlights the decision points.
Guided example: Learner completes the middle steps while the tutor provides prompts.
Transfer example: Learner applies the idea to a new context and explains the result.
lessons.practical_activity: Concept-to-application workshop followed by a short practice set.
lessons.guided_practice: Complete two examples together using the sequence: understand → plan → solve → verify.
lessons.independent_practice: Complete 5–8 questions independently and use the self-check criteria before submitting.
questions: What does review & retrieval mean in your own words?
How would you explain the idea to a classmate?
Which step requires the most care?
How can you check your answer?
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: Short formative quiz plus one application problem; target clear reasoning and 75%+ accuracy.
lessons.student_task: Prepare a mini study card: definition/rule, example, common mistake and one self-test question.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Use age/level-appropriate examples, check prerequisite gaps, and give specific feedback on reasoning.
lessons.reflection_completion: Complete: I can now ____. I still find ____ difficult. I will practise ____ tomorrow.

lessons.title: Challenge orientation & strategy

lessons.core_teaching_content: This challenge lesson develops challenge orientation & strategy for Mathematics Challenge. Begin with a short strategy briefing, then use progressively harder questions. Learners should justify methods, manage time and review errors.
examples: Warm-up: one accessible question to activate the relevant concept.

Transfer challenge: learner solves a novel problem under a short time limit.
lessons.practical_activity: Challenge ladder: warm-up → standard → advanced → one stretch question.
lessons.guided_practice: Solve two questions with the tutor, requiring the learner to state the strategy before answering.
lessons.independent_practice: Complete a timed set and classify each question as Easy / Medium / Hard after attempting it.
questions: What clue helped you choose the strategy?
Which distractor or trap could mislead a learner?
Can you solve the problem using another valid method?
How would you improve your time without sacrificing accuracy?
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: 10-question timed checkpoint; target 70%+ accuracy and a written explanation for all errors.
lessons.student_task: Prepare a personal challenge card with one solved example, one unsolved question and your strategy.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Encourage reasoning, pacing and verification; never reward guessing over justified answers.
lessons.reflection_completion: Write the strategy that worked best today and the one habit you will change in the next challenge.

examples: Warm-up: one accessible question to activate the relevant concept.

lessons.practical_activity: Challenge ladder: warm-up → standard → advanced → one stretch question.
lessons.guided_practice: Solve two questions with the tutor, requiring the learner to state the strategy before answering.

questions: What clue helped you choose the strategy?
Which distractor or trap could mislead a learner?

How would you improve your time without sacrificing accuracy?
lessons.assessment_checkpoint: 10-question timed checkpoint; target 70%+ accuracy and a written explanation for all errors.
lessons.student_task: Prepare a personal challenge card with one solved example, one unsolved question and your strategy.
lessons.tutor_guidance: Encourage reasoning, pacing and verification; never reward guessing over justified answers.
lessons.reflection_completion: Write the strategy that worked best today and the one habit you will change in the next challenge.
